corrections.caveats: Enricher: a static schedule on the triangular pair loop gives thread 0 23.4% of the pairs, so 8 threads cap near 4.27x and the book's 4.1x sits at that cap (schedule(dynamic) or a balanced split would do better). The benchmark has no UseRealTime() and Google Benchmark's default CPU timer counts only the main thread; calls take 1-5 s, so with the default 0.5 s minimum time each figure is likely a single iteration. An O(n log n) closest-pair algorithm would beat both versions (about 1M steps against 2.1B pair checks, derived). CMake sets no build type (a plain build is unoptimised); open PR #14 fixes Chapter-04 gemm build errors, so building the whole chapter may fail.

corrections.tradeoffs: Several copies of the same loop plus a runtime CPUID dispatcher (my_cpuid.h, get_best_instructions.h); larger binary, and the ct::saxpy dispatcher runs CPUID on every call rather than caching the result (CPUID is serialising and traps in virtual machines, so it can rival the roughly 300 ns of work; the dispatcher itself is never timed). x86-only intrinsics and CPUID code; my_cpuid.h tests __MSVC__ and __X86__ instead of _MSC_VER and __i386__, so it breaks plain MSVC and 32-bit GCC. The SSE4.2 build matches the default build (330 versus 329 ns), probably because SSE2 already vectorises the loop.
corrections.caveats: Enricher: built with -mavx2 but without -mfma, so the AVX2 and hand-written versions do separate multiply and add. The kernels do not check x's length (only an assert in the dispatcher). The gain is well below the vector width because the 40 KB working set is cache-bandwidth-bound. CMake sets no build type (a plain build is unoptimised); open PR #14 fixes Chapter-04 build errors.
